To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the azimuth-variance and the topography can be precisely accommodated in the time-domain image formation of general bistatic SAR data by using an appropriate coordinate system, (2) this approach is computationally efficient, and (3) it has the capability to produce images of high-quality, comparable to those of monostatic SAR
the time-domain approach can be used for general bistatic SAR, and that the subaperture processing is a good choice for the image formation.

1) a bistatic SAR system can be modelled as a monostatic SAR system with a virtual transmitter, 2) the azimuth-invariance of the monostatic SAR can be preserved, 3) the azimuth-variance and the topography of the scene can be precisely accommodated by using a suitable coordinate system, 4) the computational burden of the proposed method can be kept at a reasonable level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient and robust image formation algorithms for general bistatic SAR.
the development of a generalised SAR imaging algorithm for the precise image formation from data collected in general bistatic acquisition geometries.
the development of a new efficient bistatic SAR image processing algorithm, which is based on a subaperture processing approach and which can be applied to general bistatic SAR configurations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented time-domain image formation approach can be used as an alternative to the Fourier-based algorithms for general bistatic SAR data.
the presented algorithm is a powerful and practical implementation of the bistatic SAR imaging concept.

the time-domain image formation algorithm with the elliptic coordinate system is an efficient and robust solution for the generalised bistatic problem, which can be used for a wide variety of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general bistatic SAR, we have found a way to preserve the main properties of the well-established monostatic FFBP algorithm: azimuth-invariancy and topography-insensitiviy.

the presented algorithm is able to handle all of the effects that can be encountered in general bistatic SAR configurations, and it is therefore capable of providing high-quality images for such configurations.
, for a given bistatic SAR configuration, we have developed an efficient and practical time-domain image formation algorithm with precise accommodation of azimuth- and topography-variance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
time-domain image formation is the best option for general bistatic SAR.
, in the time domain, the precise accommodation of topography and azimuth-variance can be achieved in a very efficient way.
the time-domain approach to bistatic SAR focussing is a promising alternative for the precise accommodation of azimuth variance and topography.
